summary: Tokio Takata is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS. He held faculty posts at Otaru University of Commerce (1981–1983), Kyoto University (1983, 1997–2014), and Fudan University (2016–2022).

Tokugen Sakai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He taught at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko (1879–1882), and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida, and later in Freiburg under Husserl and Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University (1925–1943), Kyoto University (1931–1953), and Ryukoku University (1961).
Tom De Rauw works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ann Heirman and was attested as an AAP staff member at Ghent University in 2026.

Tom Ginsburg is a legal and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of California, Berkeley. He taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before joining the University of Chicago faculty around 2008.

Tom Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May. He served on the faculty at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and held a visiting chair at the University of Calgary (~2008).
Tomohiro Manabe specializes in Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2020) and as an associate professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Tomoko Makidono is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology researcher who was a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026). She also served as a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2015).

Tomoko Masuzawa specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. After studying at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara, she held faculty positions at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and the University of Michigan (from 1999).
Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post as a full-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012) and as a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
Tomoyuki Uno is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a JSPS research fellow (attested 1998) and as an associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Madras and Banaras Hindu University under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal. He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, earning a PhD from the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and William Sax. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2009).

Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Western Kentucky University. He served on the faculty at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

Torakazu Doi was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1923–1926). He later held posts at Sagami Women's University and Dokkyo University (~1964–1971).

Torkel Brekke studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Oslo and University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He held positions at the University of Oslo, PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and the MF Norwegian School of Theology (2023).

Toru Funayama specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, having studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He held academic posts at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).
